GND: Connect every GND pin on both connectors; do not leave any ground pin open. [DS §4]
PWR5: +5V main input, 4.75–5.25 V. Connect all six +5V pins (77, 79, 81, 83, 85, 87) to the same rail. [project]
Budget 1.4 A typical operating current (400 mA idle) on +5V; the real figure depends on the workload. [DS §5.3]
Loads drawn from the CM4_3.3V and CM4_1.8V outputs are not included in the CM4 current figures; add them to the +5V budget. [DS §5.4]
PWR33: CM4_3.3V output (pins 84, 86): 3.3 V ± 2.5 %, max 300 mA per pin, 600 mA total. It is off during power-off and while GLOBAL_EN is low. [DS Table 6]
On this board CM4_3.3V feeds GPIO_VREF and the status LEDs only; heavy 3.3 V loads take their own regulator from +5V. [project]
PWR18: CM4_1.8V (pins 88, 90) is not used on this board: leave both pins unconnected. [project]
GPIO: GPIO level is set by GPIO_VREF (pin 78) = 3.3 V on this board; inputs are not 5 V tolerant (absolute maximum VGPIO_VREF + 0.5 V): level-shift any 5 V source. [DS Table 3]
Keep the total load on the 28 GPIO pins below 50 mA. [DS §2.5]
Set drive strength and slew rate as low as the load allows (software setting) to reduce EMC issues. [DS §2.5]
Internal GPIO pull-up/pull-down is 47 kΩ typical (33–73 kΩ at 3.3 V); fit an external resistor where a stronger pull is needed. [DS Table 4]

Each GPIO powers up with a fixed pull-up or pull-down (shown in the pin panel); where the project note needs a defined level before software starts, fit the external pull on the baseboard. [BCM2711 §5.3]
ETH: Route the four Ethernet pairs as 100 Ω differential pairs with suitable clearance. [DS §2.2]
Match P and N within each Ethernet pair to better than 0.15 mm. [DS §2.2]
Pair-to-pair matching only needs to be better than 50 mm, so normally no inter-pair matching is required. [DS §2.2]
The PHY (BCM54210PE) corrects MDI crossover, pair skew and polarity: no pair crossing is needed. [DS §2.2]
This board links PHY-to-PHY to an Ethernet switch port, not to a MagJack; transformer or capacitive coupling is the schematic engineer's choice. [project]
SD: eMMC variant: the SD/eMMC interface (pins 57–75) is not brought out. Leave every SD pin unconnected. [project]
USB: Route USB_N/USB_P (pins 103/105) as a 90 Ω differential pair with P/N matched to better than 0.15 mm. [DS §2.4]
USB is disabled by the firmware by default; enable it with otg_mode=1 in config.txt. [DS §2.4]
The pair goes to the USB 2.0 hub upstream (2 external ports, LTE modem, spare) and to the rpiboot service port. [project]
PCIE: Route the three PCIe pairs (REFCLK, TX, RX) as 90 Ω differential pairs with suitable clearance. [DS §2.3]
Match P and N within each PCIe pair to better than 0.1 mm. No length matching between pairs is needed. [DS §2.3]
AC coupling: the CLK and TX capacitors are on the CM4; the RX pair needs external capacitors close to the device TX — on an NVMe card they are on the card. [DS §2.3]
M.2 mapping on this board: CM4 TX (pins 122/124) → PETp0/PETn0, CM4 RX (pins 116/118) ← PERp0/PERn0, REFCLK (110/112) → REFCLK+/−. [project]
PCIe_CLK_nREQ (pin 102) is mandatory: without it the CM4 does not produce the clock. Connect PCIe_nRST (pin 109) so the device is reset correctly. [DS §2.3]
Wire pin 102 to M.2 CLKREQ# and pin 109 to M.2 PERST#. [project]
CSI0: Route CSI0 (2 data lanes + clock) as 100 Ω differential pairs, P/N matched to better than 0.15 mm. [DS §2.7]
CSI0 goes to the camera FFC. The CM4IO board uses a 22-pin 0.5 mm FFC; Raspberry Pi camera modules use 15-pin 1.0 mm (adapter cable). [project]
The camera control bus is I2C0 (pins 82/80); route it to the FFC together with Camera_GPIO (pin 97). [project]
CSI1: Route CSI1 as 100 Ω differential pairs, P/N matched to better than 0.15 mm. [DS §2.7]
Only lane D0 (pins 115/117) and the clock (127/129) are used: single-lane link from the ADV7280A-M. Leave D1–D3 (121/123, 133/135, 139/141) unconnected. [project]
HDMI0: HDMI0 is not used on this board: leave all HDMI0 pins unconnected. [project]
HDMI1: HDMI1 is not used on this board: leave all HDMI1 pins unconnected. [project]
DSI0: DSI0 is not used on this board: leave all DSI0 pins unconnected. [project]
DSI1: DSI1 is not used on this board: leave all DSI1 pins unconnected. [project]
I2C0: SDA0/SCL0 (pins 82/80, BCM2711 GPIO44/45) have 1.8 kΩ pull-ups to CM4_3.3V on the CM4: add no strong external pull-ups. [DS Table 6]
Two clients on this bus: the CSI0 camera (via the FFC) and the ADV7280A-M decoder at 0x21 (ALSB high) or 0x20 (ALSB low). [project]
CTRL: All CTRL inputs (pins 20, 89, 91, 92, 93, 99) are internally pulled up: leave them floating when unused; switch only to GND (jumper, button or open-drain driver; RUN_PG through 220 Ω). [DS Table 6]
RSV: Reserved pins 76, 104, 106: do not connect anything to them. [DS Table 6]
VDAC: Composite TV-out (VDAC_COMP, pin 111) is not used on this board: leave it unconnected. [project]
ANALOG: AnalogIP0/1 (pins 96/94, MXL7704 inputs for USB-C CC): no USB-C PD on this board, leave both unconnected. [project]

15: Ethernet LED output, active low, sink ≤ 8 mA at VOL < 0.4 V: LED anode through a series resistor to CM4_3.3V (pins 84/86) — not to a baseboard rail that stays up while the CM4 is off (back-feed). [DS Table 6]
16: IEEE 1588 SYNC input, not used on this board: leave unconnected. [project]
17: Ethernet LED output, active low, sink ≤ 8 mA at VOL < 0.4 V: LED anode through a series resistor to CM4_3.3V (pins 84/86) — not to a baseboard rail that stays up while the CM4 is off (back-feed). [DS Table 6]
18: IEEE 1588 SYNC output, not used on this board: leave unconnected. [project]
19: Ethernet LED output, active low, sink ≤ 8 mA at VOL < 0.4 V: LED anode through a series resistor to CM4_3.3V (pins 84/86) — not to a baseboard rail that stays up while the CM4 is off (back-feed). [DS Table 6]
20: Leave floating (100 kΩ internal pull-up to CM4_3.3V, VIL < 0.8 V) or ground it to write-protect the bootloader EEPROM. [DS Table 6]
To write-protect, EEPROM_nWP must be low before power-up. [DS §5.1]
Final products should pull it low so end users cannot change the EEPROM contents. [DS §2.18]
21: Active-low activity LED: 20 mA max, 5 V tolerant, VOL < 0.4 V. [DS Table 6]
This LED flashes an error pattern if boot fails; keep it visible for service. [DS §2.16]
24: Fan tachometer input: open-collector output, add a pull-up on the baseboard — the internal 47 kΩ is too weak for a long cable. [project]
26: TX2 power-switch enable: pull-down at boot keeps the module off; same switch-gate pull-down as TX1 (pin 50). [project]
49: Fan PWM (PWM0 channel 0). Low at boot: if the fan must run before software starts, add a pull-up at the driver input. [project]
50: TX1 power-switch enable (12 V, up to 2 W RF): pull-down at boot keeps the module off; add a pull-down at the switch gate too. [project]
51: Service console RXD0, on the same 3-pin header as pin 55. [project]
55: Service console TXD0: 3-pin header (GND, TXD, RXD) with pin 51, 3.3 V. [project]
56: SCL1 sensor bus: 1.8 kΩ pull-up already on the CM4 — do not add strong external pull-ups. [project]
58: SDA1 sensor bus: 1.8 kΩ pull-up already on the CM4 — do not add strong external pull-ups. [project]
78: Tie GPIO_VREF to CM4_3.3V (pins 84 and 86). It must not float and must not be grounded: the CM4 does not start without it. [DS Table 6]
80: Route to the CSI0 camera FFC and to the ADV7280A-M SCL (U1 pin 31). [sdtv2csi]
82: Route to the CSI0 camera FFC and to the ADV7280A-M SDA (U1 pin 30). [sdtv2csi]
89: WL_nDisable: 1.8 kΩ internal pull-up to CM4_3.3V; can be left floating. [DS Table 6]
Tie or drive low to keep the wireless module powered down; as an input, high = module powered up. [DS §2.1.1]
Fit a jumper to GND so Wi-Fi can be disabled when the ELRS 2.4 GHz module is nearby. [project]
91: BT_nDisable: 1.8 kΩ internal pull-up to CM4_3.3V; can be left floating. [DS Table 6]
Tie or drive low to keep the Bluetooth module powered down; as an input, high = module powered up. [DS §2.1.2]
92: Reset input: pull low to GND through a 220 Ω resistor (button or open-drain driver). Internal 10 kΩ pull-up to +3.3V. [DS Table 6]
As an output, high = power good and CPU running. Drive a run LED through a buffer, not directly. [project]
Resetting via RUN_PG closes no open files; use it with caution. [DS §2.14]
93: Low forces boot from a USB host (rpiboot) instead of eMMC; for that it must be low within 2 ms of +5V rising. [DS §5.1]
Internal 10 kΩ pull-up to +3.3V; leave floating if unused. [DS Table 6]
Fit a jumper or button to GND: this is the path for eMMC flashing and recovery. [DS §6.2]
95: Optional power LED: active-low output that must be buffered (transistor) — it cannot drive an LED directly. [DS §2.17]
97: Camera_GPIO: typically used to shut the camera down. Reassigning this pin is not recommended. CM4_3.3V signalling. [DS Table 6]
Route to the CSI0 camera FFC. [project]
99: Drive low to power the CM4 off; internal 100 kΩ pull-up to +5V. [DS Table 6]
With GLOBAL_EN low the CM4 draws 15 µA (lowest power state). [DS Table 5]
After a software shutdown hold it low for more than 1 ms to restart the power system; pull it low only once the OS has shut down. [DS §2.13]
Driven open-drain only, by the Ethernet-reboot circuit (independent of the CM4); the 3.3 V and 1.8 V outputs drop while low, release = cold start. [project]
100: Output only: low during reset, high (CM4_3.3V) once the CPU has started to boot. [DS Table 6]
Optional: use it to reset peripherals such as the USB hub. [project]
101: Tie USB_OTG_ID to GND for a fixed host (or fixed device) role; internally pulled up; the OS driver must match. [DS §2.4]
rpiboot needs a direct USB path CM4 ↔ PC in device mode: a switch or jumper between the hub upstream and the service port (schematic engineer's choice). [project]
102: 3.3 V input, low = clock requested; internally pulled up. [DS Table 6]
109: Wire to M.2 PERST# (clean SSD reset). [project]
110: PCIe clock out positive, 100 MHz → M.2 REFCLK+ (pair with pin 112). [project]
112: PCIe clock out negative, 100 MHz → M.2 REFCLK− (pair with pin 110). [project]
115: CSI1 D0− from ADV7280A-M D0N (U1 pin 10), pair with pin 117. Single-lane CSI-2 link. [sdtv2csi]
116: Wire from M.2 PERp0 (the SSD transmitter), pair with pin 118. [project]
117: CSI1 D0+ from ADV7280A-M D0P (U1 pin 9), pair with pin 115. [sdtv2csi]
118: Wire from M.2 PERn0, pair with pin 116. [project]
122: Wire to M.2 PETp0, pair with pin 124. [project]
124: Wire to M.2 PETn0, pair with pin 122. [project]
127: CSI1 clock− from ADV7280A-M CLKN (U1 pin 12), pair with pin 129. [sdtv2csi]
129: CSI1 clock+ from ADV7280A-M CLKP (U1 pin 11), pair with pin 127. [sdtv2csi]

general.title: Mechanical & connectors
items: Module 55 × 40 mm, 4.7 mm deep; PCB 1.2 mm ± 10 %. Four M2.5 mounting holes inset 3.5 mm from the module edges. [DS §3.1]
Two 100-pin Hirose DF40 receptacles on the baseboard: DF40C-100DS-0.4V for 1.5 mm stacking (0 mm clearance under the CM4) or DF40HC(3.0)-100DS-0.4V for 3.0 mm stacking (1.5 mm clearance). [DS §3.1]
Mated height: 5.078 mm with the 1.5 mm stack, 6.578 mm with the 3.0 mm stack. BCM2711 height including solder balls is 2.378 ± 0.11 mm. [DS §3.1]

With the 1.5 mm stack there is 0 mm clearance under the CM4: place no components on the baseboard inside the module footprint. With the 3.0 mm stack, components under the module must be lower than 1.5 mm. [DS §3.1]

The board drawing (CM4 viewed from the top, connectors on its underside) is also the baseboard top-view footprint — no mirroring. Pin 1 is at the right end of both connectors; confirm the pin numbering against the DF40 receptacle drawing. [DS Fig. 4]

Connector axes 3 mm from the long edges (J1 y = 3 mm, J2 y = 37 mm), centred at x = 25 mm from the antenna edge; body approximately 22 × 3 mm — take pad geometry and exact placement from the DF40 receptacle footprint. [DS Fig. 4]
Component placement on the CM4 may change between revisions; maximum component heights and PCB thickness are kept. Use the STEP file from the CM4 design data for guidance only. [DS §3.1]

general.title: Power & sequencing
items: Single +5V supply: it must rise monotonically to 4.75 V and stay above 4.75 V during operation. [DS §5.1]
Apply no power to any pin before the +5V rail is applied. [DS §5.1]
During power-down/off no pin may have an external voltage applied, or the next power-up may be prevented. [DS §4]
Power-up order: +5V → GLOBAL_EN (internal RC delay) → 3.3 V → 1.8 V at least 1 ms later → RUN_PG at least 10 ms later → EXT_nRESET at least 1 s later. [DS §5.1]
Power-down: shut the OS down, then remove +5V or pull GLOBAL_EN low. During shutdown the 1.8 V rail is discharged before the 3.3 V rail. [DS §5.2]
If CM4_3.3V feeds anything besides GPIO_VREF, on surprise power loss (+5V below 4.5 V) it must never fall below CM4_1.8V; otherwise add circuitry that disconnects the 3.3 V load. [DS §4]
Supply check with GLOBAL_EN low: +5V above 4.75 V (ideally above 4.9 V) under a 2 A load including noise; CM4 3.3 V and 1.8 V rails both below 200 mV (no back-feed). [DS §6.1]

general.title: Boot, reset & service
items: nRPIBOOT (pin 93) and EEPROM_nWP (pin 20) are grounded by jumpers on the CM4IO board (§6.2, §6.4): fit jumpers or buttons to GND here. [DS §6.2]
The bootloader EEPROM can only be updated via usbboot or self-update: keep the rpiboot path (nRPIBOOT jumper plus a direct USB device path to a PC) reachable in the field. [DS §6.3]
Service console on this board: UART0 on a 3-pin header (GND, TXD, RXD), 3.3 V; the only UART the bootloader writes to. [project]

general.title: High-speed differential pairs
items: Impedance: 90 Ω differential for PCIe (REFCLK, TX, RX) and USB 2.0; 100 Ω differential for Ethernet, CSI, HDMI and DSI. [DS §4.1]
On the CM4 every pair is P/N-matched to better than 0.05 mm; the CM4-side track-length differences between pairs (Tables 7–8) are shown per pin in the pin panel. [DS §4.1]

general.title: GPIO & low-speed interfaces
items: UARTs on this board: UART0 console (55/51), UART2 GPS (36/35), UART3 CRSF TX1 (54/34, RTS 37), UART4 CRSF TX2 (39/40, RTS 38), UART5 servo bus (31/28); all 3.3 V. [project]
GPIO0/1 (pins 36/35) are UART2, not the HAT I2C: add force_eeprom_read=0 and disable_poe_fan=1 to config.txt to stop the boot-time EEPROM probe. [DS §2.10]
Single-wire buses need baseboard hardware: CRSF TX1/TX2 a direction buffer plus inverter (direction from RTS3/RTS4), the ST3025 servo bus an automatic-direction buffer. [project]
SPI6 to the video receivers: MOSI on pin 27, SCLK on pin 25, one LE (chip-select) GPIO per receiver on pins 46, 47, 45, 41. [project]

general.title: Wi-Fi & RF
items: No copper or other metal on any baseboard layer under the antenna: copper-free area minimum 6.5 × 11 mm, ideally at least 8 × 15 mm (smaller degrades 2.4 GHz most). [DS §3.1]
The antenna area is at the short edge of the module: x = 0–6.5 mm, y = 10.5–21.5 mm on the board drawing (CM4 viewed from the top); hatched on the page. [DS Fig. 4]

Keep at least 10 mm clearance around the PCB antenna; any nearby metal must have cut-outs; orient the antenna toward the edge of the plastic enclosure. The designer must check the performance. [DS §3.1]
Use the external antenna where possible: a standard U.FL connector is on the module. [DS §3.1]
U.FL connector on the module at x = 2.57 mm from the antenna edge, y = 9.0 mm from the J1 (top) edge — same axes as the antenna keep-out. [DS Fig. 4]
Antenna selection is fixed at boot in config.txt: dtparam=ant1 = PCB antenna, dtparam=ant2 = external antenna. [DS §2.1]

general.title: Thermal
items: Operating temperature −20…85 °C, non-condensing. [DS §3.2]
The BCM2711 throttles its clock to keep the die below 85 °C; if it cannot, the case temperature rises above 85 °C. Keep the ambient for the other CM4 devices inside the operating range. [DS §3.2]
The CM4 has less passive heat sinking than a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B and may run warmer despite dissipating less, so a thermal solution may be needed. [DS §3.2]
BCM2711 15 × 15 mm centred at (31.99, 23.03) mm on the board drawing: centre the heatsink or fan cut-out there. [DS Fig. 4]
Fan: PWM0 on GPIO18 (pin 49), tachometer on GPIO26 (pin 24) with an external pull-up. [project]
Optimal RF performance is between −20 °C and +75 °C; keep the Wi-Fi module below 75 °C where possible. [DS §3.2]

general.title: Video decoder ADV7280A-M (project)
items: ADV7280A-M on CSI1, one data lane: D0P/D0N (U1 pins 9/10) → CM4 pins 117/115, CLKP/CLKN (U1 pins 11/12) → pins 129/127. [sdtv2csi]
I2C: SDA/SCL (U1 pins 30/31) → CM4 SDA0/SCL0 (pins 82/80). ALSB (pin 29) via 4.7 kΩ pull-up (R20) with a DNP pull-down (R21): high = address 0x21, low = 0x20. [sdtv2csi]
Power: NJM12888F18 LDO, 3.3 V → 1.8 V for AVDD, DVDD, MVDD, PVDD, each through a 600 Ω ferrite bead with 0.1 µF + 10 µF; DVDDIO = 3.3 V. Crystal Y1: ABM8G 28.63636 MHz, 2 × 20 pF. [sdtv2csi]
Analogue inputs AIN1–AIN8: each VINx → 24 Ω series → 0.1 µF AC coupling → AINx, with 51 Ω to GND at the input. Inputs arrive on a 2×8 pin header (VIDEO_IN). [sdtv2csi]
~RESET (pin 28): 4.7 kΩ pull-up + 4.7 µF to GND (RC power-on reset); ~PWRDWN (pin 32): 4.7 kΩ pull-up; ~INTRQ and GPO0–GPO2: test points only. No CM4 GPIO is used. [sdtv2csi]
Software: dtoverlay=adv728x-m,adv7280m=1 (default address 0x21; addr=0x20 if ALSB low); the overlay targets CSI1 and I2C0 (pins 82/80). [project]
I2C0 is shared with the CSI0 camera; a CSI0 camera needs a custom overlay variant using i2c_csi_dsi (stock cam0 variants expect I2C on GPIO0/1, which are UART2 here). [project]
The CVBS 4→1 switch + K7 encoder path stays in parallel; GPIO6/GPIO10 (pins 30/44) remain CVBS_SEL0/1. [project]
